why: A spanning query is checked against EACH corpus's own ontology, and `upstream`'s `concept` declares no properties at all — so `claim_tag` typechecks here and does not there. That is not a defect in the query and not a failed run: the dependency is excluded with the reason, as a diagnostic, and the local rows still come back. A shared class name is not agreement, which this case is the sharpest statement of — two corpora both declaring `concept` mean different things by it, and one of them cannot be asked this question. A server that failed the whole run would make a caller's answer depend on what happens to be installed; one that excluded the corpus silently would report a local-only answer under `"scope": "across"`, which is the reading `scope` exists to prevent.
